column1: How many households have received cash transfers?
column2: About 15 million vulnerable households reached cumulatively, according to the President's July 2026 address.
column3: Direct support for the poorest families, paid into their accounts.

column1: What new World Bank-backed programmes were launched in July 2026?
column2: $3.05bn in total: NG-CARES ($1.25bn for farmers and small businesses), SOLID ($300m for displaced people and host communities) and HOPE ($1.5bn for primary healthcare, schools and ward-level services).
column3: Support reaching farmers, small traders, clinics and schools at ward level.

column1: How many homes are planned in the Renewed Hope City in Karsana, Abuja?
column2: 3,112 housing units, now under construction, part of Renewed Hope Cities and Estates across the country.
column3: More decent, affordable homes for workers and young families.

column2: The MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund: ₦150 billion to make mortgages more available and affordable.
column3: It helps working Nigerians own homes instead of paying rent forever.

column2: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, with ₦50 billion so working Nigerians can buy essentials like solar systems, laptops or vehicles and pay over time.
column3: Credit for ordinary people, not just big businesses.

column1: How much has gone into student loans (NELFUND)?
column2: ₦375 billion across more than 1.67 million loans; tuition is paid directly to schools and upkeep to students.
column3: No bright student should drop out because of fees.
